modules.name: minisvc.cli
modules.purpose: CLI bootstrap entry point: loads settings, constructs the repository, initializes the SQLite schema, and reports readiness.

modules.name: minisvc.config
modules.purpose: Reads MINISVC_DB and MINISVC_READONLY from an environment mapping into immutable Settings.

modules.name: minisvc.storage.repo
modules.purpose: SQLite-backed order persistence, schema creation, inserts, and lookups.

modules.name: minisvc.api.routes
modules.purpose: Registers POST and GET order routes on an injected app and repository.

modules.name: minisvc.api.handlers
modules.purpose: Transforms request payloads into Orders and coordinates create/read repository operations and response shaping.

modules.name: minisvc.audit
modules.purpose: Builds in-memory order event dictionaries; it does not persist them.

modules.name: minisvc
modules.purpose: Package marker/export declaration, not business logic.

modules.name: minisvc.api
modules.purpose: API package marker; no runtime business logic.

modules.name: minisvc.storage
modules.purpose: Storage package marker; no runtime business logic.

key_functions.role: Maps environment values to Settings; defaults DB to orders.sqlite and readonly to false.
Bootstraps configuration and SQLite schema; returns 0 after printing readiness.
Stores the database path as a pathlib.Path.
Creates orders(order_id primary key, customer, total_cents) if absent.
Inserts an Order into SQLite; duplicate keys and database errors propagate.
Queries by order_id and reconstructs an Order or returns None.
Validates only by direct key access/conversion, saves the order, and returns a created response plus transient event data.
Reads an order and returns missing/ok response plus transient read event data.
Binds POST /orders and GET /orders/<order_id> using lambdas over the injected repository.
Constructs an event dictionary; no database write occurs.

runtime_flows.name: CLI startup
steps: main calls repo.init_schema(), opening SQLite and creating the orders table if needed.
main prints the database path and returns 0.

runtime_flows.name: HTTP create-order
steps: An external HTTP app calls register_routes(app, repo).
POST /orders dispatches through the registered lambda to create_order(payload, repo).
create_order reads order_id and customer and converts total_cents with int(), constructing Order.
OrderRepository.save inserts the row into SQLite and commits on context-manager exit.
order_event(order, 'created') builds an in-memory event dictionary.
The handler returns status, order_id, and the event; there is no retry, readonly check, or audit-table write.
